questions.question:
Choose the idiom from the given alternatives that best matches the following definition:

"A person or thing that appears to be powerful, threatening, or impressive but is actually weak, ineffective, or lacks the power to back up its claims."
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 4** i.e. **Paper Tiger**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **“Paper Tiger”** refers to a person or thing that appears to be powerful, threatening, or impressive but is actually weak, ineffective, or lacks the power to back up its claims. (कागजी शेर)
 
 
• **Example:** The dictator claimed to have a powerful army, but it turned out to be nothing more than a paper tiger.
 
 
• The idiom is often used to describe situations or entities that are overhyped but lack substance or strength.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Paper Tiger**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **A Flash in the Pan** (क्षणिक सफलता): Refers to something or someone that initially shows great promise but fails to deliver or last.
 
 
• **Example:** His music career was just a flash in the pan; he disappeared after one hit song.
 
 
 
• **A Dark Horse** (छुपा रुस्तम): Refers to a person who is not well-known but unexpectedly emerges as a strong contender or winner.
 
 
• **Example:** Nobody expected her to win the competition; she was a real dark horse.
 
 
 
• **A Stalking Horse** (छल का माध्यम): Refers to a person or thing used to disguise someone's true intentions.
 
 
• **Example:** The proposal was just a stalking horse to divert attention from their actual plan.

options.text: To remain in a state of constant anxiety or nervous anticipation.
To maintain an open and hospitable invitation for someone to visit at any time.
To narrowly escape a disastrous situation by a very small margin.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 2** i.e. "To maintain an open and hospitable invitation for someone to visit at any time."

• **Example:** Our grandmother always leaves the latch-string out for family members who want to visit her.

• **Example:** The villagers left the latch-string out for travelers passing through, offering them food and shelter.

questions.question:
**Direction: Which of the following is the correct active form of the sentence-**

The bridge was considered a menace to navigation by the boat owners.

options.text: The boat owners have considered the bridge a menace to navigation.
The boat owners had considered the bridge a menace to navigation.
The boat owners considered the bridge a menace to navigation.
The boat owners consider the bridge a menace to navigation.

questions.solution:
The correct answer: **'The boat owners considered the bridge a menace to navigation.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 
• The given sentence is in Passive Voice. It is in Simple Past Tense.
 
• As per the given question, we must change it to Active Voice. 
 
• The structure of the given sentence is as follows:
 
 
• Subject + V2 + Object. (Active Voice)
 
• Subject (objective case)+ was/were + V3 + Object (subjective case). (Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• **Example:**
 
 
• *Their cousin showed them some rare photographs. (Active Voice)*
 
• *They were shown some rare photographs by their cousin. (Passive Voice)*
 
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is 'the bridge'.​​
 
• The object of the given sentence is 'the boat owners'. 
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject.
 
• And 'was considered' will be changed into 'considered'. 
 
• The preposition 'by' will be removed. 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Correct sentence: *The boat owners considered the bridge a menace to navigation.*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The company will release the new product next month.

options.text: The new product will be released by the company next month.
The new product will release by the company next month.
The new product will be releasing by the company next month.
The new product is released by the company next month.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **The new product will be released by the company next month**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **subject** of the Active Voice is changed into the **object** of the Passive voice. Also, the **object **of the Active Voice is changed into the **subject** of the Passive Voice.
 
• The usage of a **helping verb** is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.
 
• The preposition **“by”** is used before the object made in Passive Voice. However, it is optional in some cases.
 
• The Active voice in this question is in **Future Indefinite**. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in the **Future Indefinite**.
 
• The format of Active voice is: **Subject + shall/will + V1 + Object**.
 
• Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: **Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + shall/will + be + made + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).**
 
• For example:
 
 
• He will complete the assignment. (Active Voice)
 
• The assignment will be completed by him. (Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• The options except (1) don’t follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: ***The new product will be released by the company next month.***

• The way in which an interrogative sentence is converted into its active voice is: 
 
 
• Wh-word + helping verb + subject (object of passive voice) + adverb (not) + Ist form of the main verb + object (subject of the passive voice) + adverb of time?
 
 
 
• The tense remains the same as the passive voice.
 
• Here, the simple past tense is used.

questions.question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error:

(1) Had the archaeological conservators not been so meticulous in their preservation of the papyrus scrolls / (2) discovered within the volcanic ash of the Herculaneum villa, / (3) the text of the Epicurean treatises would have likely been lost to history, / (4) thereby deprive modern scholars of their most significant insights into Hellenistic philosophy.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. thereby deprive .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in part (4) of the sentence: **"thereby deprive."**
 
• The phrase "thereby deprive" is grammatically incorrect because it uses the base form "deprive" instead of the correct verb form "depriving."
 
• The word "thereby" is typically followed by a gerund (-ing form), as it describes the result or consequence of an action.

Correct sentence: *Had the archaeological conservators not been so meticulous in their preservation of the papyrus scrolls discovered within the volcanic ash of the Herculaneum villa, the text of the Epicurean treatises would have likely been lost to history, thereby depriving modern scholars of their most significant insights into Hellenistic philosophy.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Usage of "thereby":**
 
 
• "Thereby" is used to show the result or consequence of an action.
 
• It is typically followed by a gerund (verb ending in -ing).
 
• Example: He improved his skills, thereby increasing his chances of success.
 
 
 
• **Common Errors:**
 
 
• Using the base form of the verb instead of the gerund after "thereby."
 
• Example of Incorrect Usage: She worked hard, thereby achieve her goals.
 
• Corrected Example: She worked hard, thereby achieving her goals.
 
 
</ul

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that rectifies the underlined group of words in the given sentence.

If it __**were me who had been assigned**__ to the high-stakes project, I would have ensured that every contingency plan was rigorously tested.

options.text: was me who had been assigned
was I who had been assigned
would be I who was assigned
were I who had been assigned

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. were I who had been assigned .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence uses a subjunctive mood, which is common in hypothetical or conditional contexts.
 
• The subjunctive form of the verb "to be" is "were" when referring to hypothetical or unreal situations.
 
• In formal English, when the subject of the clause is inverted (e.g., "Were I" instead of "If I were"), this construction is used to emphasize the conditional nature.
 
• The correct form of the sentence is: *If it **were I** who had been assigned to the high-stakes project, I would have ensured that every contingency plan was rigorously tested.*

Correct sentence: *If it **were I** who had been assigned to the high-stakes project, I would have ensured that every contingency plan was rigorously tested*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subjunctive Mood:**
 
 
• The subjunctive is used to express wishes, hypothetical situations, or conditions contrary to fact.
 
• Example: If I **were** a millionaire, I would buy a yacht.
 
 
 
• **Inversion in Conditional Sentences:**
 
 
• In formal English, the "if" clause can be replaced with inversion for emphasis or stylistic effect.
 
• Example: Were she to arrive on time, we would start the meeting immediately (equivalent to "If she were to arrive on time").
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Based on the passage, which of the following best characterizes the author’s stance on AI in physical activities?

options.text: Enthusiastic support for the democratization of elite coaching.
Skepticism regarding the accuracy of biometric data collection.
Concern over the alienation of athletes from their own bodies.
Objective indifference toward the inevitable rise of automation.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To identify the **author's stance**, we must look beyond the initial facts and examine the "tonal shift" that occurs in the second paragraph.
 
• While the first paragraph mentions some benefits (democratized coaching, injury prevention), the second paragraph is dominated by critical language: **"erosion of somatic autonomy," "quantitative fetishism," "laboratory of surveillance,"** and **"risk alienating the athlete."**
 
• The author concludes by warning that AI threatens to replace the **"primal, unmediated connection between mind and muscle"** with a **"simulation of health."** This clearly indicates a deep **concern** that humans are losing touch with their own biological signals.
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 1:** This is a **partial truth**. While the author acknowledges democratization, it is not their final or primary stance; it is the "counter-point" used to set up their main criticism.
 
• **Option 2:** The author does not question the **accuracy** of the data (they acknowledge it can optimize efficiency); they question the **value** of relying on it so heavily.
 
• **Option 4:** The author uses highly emotive and critical vocabulary (fetishism, alienation, threat), which is the opposite of **indifference**.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **3**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In high-difficulty exams, the author's stance is often found in the "Conclusion" or the "But/However" section. When a passage is split between Pros and Cons, the section with the more sophisticated or intense vocabulary (like "somatic autonomy") usually represents the author's true perspective.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Somatic Autonomy:** The right of an individual to have self-determination over their own physical body.
 
• **Unmediated:** Without any intervening medium or influence; direct.
 
• **Subsumed:** Included or absorbed into something else.
 
• **Fetishism:** In this context, an excessive or irrational commitment to a particular idea (quantitative data).

questions.question: In the phrase "quantitative fetishism," what is the most accurate meaning of the word "fetishism"?

options.text: A digital record of physical health

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To determine the meaning of **"fetishism"** in this context, we must examine the surrounding text: **"This quantitative fetishism often overlooks the qualitative nuances... the psychological grit that cannot be fully encapsulated by a heart-rate variability coefficient."**
 
• The author is criticizing the **"relentless pursuit of data-driven perfection."** In sociological and psychological terms, a **fetish** is an object or idea that is given **irrational or excessive devotion** or importance beyond its actual value.
 
• Therefore, **"quantitative fetishism"** refers to an **irrational obsession with numbers** (metrics, data, coefficients) at the expense of human experience and intuition.
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 2:** A "scientific method" is usually described as objective and balanced; "fetishism" implies a lack of balance and a move into the irrational.
 
• **Option 3:** While the passage mentions "surveillance," that is a separate point regarding computer vision and privacy, not the definition of fetishism.
 
• **Option 4:** A "digital record" is a neutral tool; the term fetishism describes the **human attitude** toward that record, not the record itself.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **1**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In high-level Reading Comprehension, words like "fetishism" or "obsession" are used to indicate a **negative bias** by the author. When an author pairs "quantitative" with a word like "fetishism," they are arguing that we are relying **too much** on numbers and losing the "qualitative" human element.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Quantitative:** Relating to, measuring, or measured by the quantity of something rather than its quality.
 
• **Qualitative:** Relating to, measuring, or measured by the quality of something (feelings, experience) rather than its quantity.
 
• **Subsumed:** Included or absorbed into something else.
 
• **Encapsulated:** Expressed the essential features of something succinctly.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the word "deleterious" as used in the passage?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the passage, the word **"deleterious"** is used in the context of **"suboptimal biomechanics."**
 
• The text explains that AI is used to **"mitigate"** (reduce or lessen) these effects. Since the goal is to prevent injuries and move toward "injury-free longevity," it follows that the effects being mitigated are **harmful or damaging**.
 
• In English, **deleterious** is a formal term meaning causing harm or damage, often in a subtle or unexpected way.
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 2:** "Conducive to physical growth" is a positive effect; we would not want to "mitigate" something that helps us grow.
 
• **Option 3:** While the passage mentions "cadence" and "speed," deleterious refers to the **quality** of the impact, not the velocity.
 
• **Option 4:** The effects mentioned are physical and biological (related to the runner's gait and injury), so they are **practical**, not "strictly theoretical."
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **1**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In high-level exams, vocabulary is often tested through **contextual logic**. Even if you didn't know the definition of "deleterious," the word "mitigate" (to make less severe) acts as a structural signpost indicating that the following word must represent something **negative**.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mitigate:** To make something bad less severe, serious, or painful.
 
• **Suboptimal:** Being below the highest level or standard, or not as good as it could be.
 
• **Visceral:** Relating to deep inward feelings rather than to the intellect; "gut feeling."
 
• **Subsumed:** Included or absorbed into something else.

questions.question:
Identify the voice of the following sentence extracted from the passage:

*"...it is increasingly moderated by generative models that synthesize kinetic data..."*
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To identify the voice of a sentence, we look at the relationship between the subject and the action.
 
• In the sentence: *"...it **is increasingly moderated by** generative models..."*: 
 
 
• The subject **"it"** (referring to the runner's gait) is not performing the action; it is receiving the action.
 
• The phrase follows the standard passive construction: **Be-verb (is) + Past Participle (moderated)**.
 
• The actual performer of the action (the agent) is introduced by the preposition **"by"** (generative models).
 
 
 
• **Passive Voice** is used here to emphasize the "gait" (the result) rather than the "models" (the cause).
 
• Why other options are incorrect: 
 
 
• **Option 1:** In **Active Voice**, the models would perform the action directly: "Generative models increasingly moderate it."
 
• **Option 3:** **Causative Voice** involves someone causing someone else to do something (e.g., "I had the models moderate my gait").
 
• **Option 4:** **Reflexive Voice** is when the subject and object are the same (e.g., "The runner corrected himself").
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **2**.

 

**Analytical Insight:** *In advanced Reading Comprehension, academic passages often favor the **Passive Voice** to maintain a formal, objective, and "scientific" tone. When you see **"is/am/are/was/were + V3 + by,"** it is a definitive marker for Passive Voice.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Deleterious:** Causing harm or damage.
 
• **Paradigm Shift:** A fundamental change in approach or underlying assumptions.
 
• **Somatic Autonomy:** The right of an individual to have self-determination over their own body.
 
• **Haptic Feedback:** The use of touch (like vibrations) to communicate with users of technology.
